newsitem.title: INDIA: Bank of Nova Scotia to expand Indian operations.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Nova Scotia to expand Indian operations.

text.p: Canada's Bank of Nova Scotia plans to step up operations in India and is setting up its third local branch early next year, an official said on Wednesday.
"We have received Reserve Bank of India licence to set up a new branch in Coimbatore," Bhaskar Desai, vice president at the bank's Bombay office, told Reuters.
The bank now has branches in New Delhi and Bombay. Desai said he expected the new branch in Coimbatore in south India to be operational by early 1997.

He said the Coimbatore branch would focus on trade and corporate finance. Coimbatore is a bustling industrial city and neighbouring towns Tirupur and Erode are major export centres for textile and engineering industries.
"We run substantial export assets on our books," Desai said.
Of late, the bank has also been focusing on foreign currency loans for Indian companies. "We have an appetite for Indian risk and the expertise to do large loans," Desai said.
The bank has received the mandate to raise a $75 million loan for Indian textile firm Arvind Mills which is expected to hit the market in the next few weeks, he said.
It recently lead managed and underwrote a $75 million syndicated loan for India's largest truck maker Tata Engineering and Locomotive Company Ltd.
The bank also jointly lead managed a $115 million loan for engineering and construction giant Larsen & Toubro.
Bank of Nova Scotia set up its Indian operations in 1985.
"The bank has appointed a senior vice president for the Indian subcontinent, based in New Delhi, with a strong India focus," Desai said. "We should see a lot more action as time passes."
